title: Deep peptide recognition profiling decodes TCR specificity and enables disease-associated antigen discovery
one_line: Combines ~10^9-member yeast-displayed peptide libraries with fine-tuned protein language models to build deep peptide recognition profiles (PRPs) for 21 HLA-B*27:05-restricted patient TCRs, then uses them to predict T cell activation and discover candidate autoantigens.
key_claims: High-throughput yeast display of ~1 billion 9-mer peptides (anchors fixed: arginine at P2, proline at P8) generated deep PRPs for 21 TCRs from ankylosing spondylitis and acute anterior uveitis patients, which recognize peptides almost exclusively via CDR3\u03b2.
pLMs (transformer encoder plus CNN feature fusion) fine-tuned on PRPs outperformed AlphaFold3 and tFold-TCR at predicting T cell activation.

Functional clustering of TCRs by Jensen-Shannon divergence of PRPs was largely independent of sequence metrics (CDR3\u03b2 edit distance, TCRdist), so sequence-dissimilar TCRs can share convergent ligand preferences.
Proteome-wide model screening nominated a PSG5-derived peptide as a candidate autoantigen, validated in vitro by CD69 upregulation on CD8+ T cells from HLA-B27-positive patients.

Leave-one-out cross-validation showed generalization to held-out TCRs correlates with PRP functional distance, not sequence similarity; a Mahalanobis distance in the model embedding space flags out-of-distribution TCRs as a confidence metric.
limitations: Fixing P2 arginine and P8 proline anchors yields a reductionist library that does not fully represent the natural peptide repertoire.
Authors acknowledge the alpha chain modulates response magnitude, so a CDR3\u03b2-centric model may not generalize to other HLA contexts.
PSG5 validation is in vitro activation-marker readout only; no in vivo evidence that it drives disease pathogenesis.
Only 21 patient-derived TCRs within a single HLA allele (B*27:05) were profiled.
Model comparisons to AlphaFold3/tFold-TCR were in silico benchmarks, not prospective experimental head-to-head.
open_questions: Does PSG5-reactive T cell recognition actually drive spinal or ocular inflammation in vivo in HLA-B27 patients?
Does the platform generalize when alpha chains are varied or to other HLA alleles with less anchor-dominated grooves?
Would unconstrained (non-fixed-anchor) libraries reveal recognition modes missed by the P2/P8-fixed design?
Can Mahalanobis-guided selection of functionally distant TCRs be shown prospectively to improve model coverage per experiment?
